In [[mathematical logic]], an '''effective Polish space''' is a [[complete metric space|complete]] [[separable space|separable]] [[metric space]] that has a [[computable presentation]]. Such spaces are studied in [[effective descriptive set theory]] and in [[constructive analysis]].  In particular, standard examples of [[Polish space]]s such as the  [[real line]], the [[Cantor set]] and the [[Baire space (set theory)|Baire space]] are all effective Polish spaces.

== Definition ==

An effective Polish space is a complete separable metric space ''X'' with metric ''d'' such that there is a countable dense set ''C'' = (''c''<sub>0</sub>, ''c''<sub>1</sub>,...) that makes the following two [[relation (logic)|relations]] on <math>\mathbb{N}^4</math> computable (Moschovakis 2009:96-7):
:<math>P(i,j,k,m) \equiv \left\{ d(c_i,c_j) \leq \frac{m}{k+1} \right\}</math>
:<math>Q(i,j,k,m) \equiv \left\{ d(c_i,c_j) < \frac{m}{k+1} \right\}</math>
